results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with splittable and segregated routing
results.quote: Theorem 1. When \tau=SS, the min-congestion reconfigurable network problem has a polynomial-time 2-approximation algorithm.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with splittable and segregated routing
results.quote: Theorem 4. For \tau=SS, the min-congestion reconfigurable network problem (MCRN) is APX-complete, even if the demands D are uniform in size and the graph G_D induced by D is acyclic and bipartite, e.g., a 3D matching.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with splittable and segregated routing, single source/destination demands
results.quote: Theorem 3. When \tau=SS, if the demands D have a single source (resp., dest.), the MCRN problem is polynomial-time solvable.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with unsplittable and segregated routing
results.quote: Theorem 2. If the min-congestion multi-commodity unsplittable flow problem has a \rho\text{-approximation algorithm based on rounding techniques on its LP solution, e.g., }\rho=O(\log m/\log\log m) [32], then the MCRN problem with \tau=US can be approximated by 2\rho.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with unsplittable and segregated routing
results.quote: Thus, the lower bound \Omega(\log m/\log\log m) [34] on approximating the min-congestion of multi-commodity unsplittable flow problem is also an approximation lower bound for the MCRN problem with \tau=US.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with non-segregated routing (splittable or unsplittable), single source/destination demands
results.quote: Theorem 6. When \tau\in\{SN,UN\}, given demands D of a single source (resp., destination), the MCRN problem cannot be approximated better than \Omega(c_{\max}/c_{\min}) unless P=NP.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with non-segregated routing (splittable or unsplittable), single source/destination demands, uniform capacities
results.quote: Theorem 7. When \tau\in\{SN,UN\}, the MRCN problem remains NP-hard for demands of a single source (resp., destination) and uniform capacities.

results.problem: Min-Congestion Reconfigurable Network Problem (MCRN) with non-segregated routing (splittable or unsplittable), single commodity demand, uniform capacities
results.quote: Theorem 8. For \tau\in\{SN,UN\}, given a single-commodity demand and uniform capacities, the MCRN problem is polynomial-time solvable.
